Post office CEO Mark Barnes

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Can Maverick Businessman Mark Barnes turn his vision for the ailing post office into a reality

Summary:
Mark Barnes, maverick businessman, social commentator, former chairperson of Purple Capital, before that one of the bright boys at Standard Bank – white South African Male – now the new CEO of the post office. How the hell did that happen?


Further information:
The post office is in trouble – well more than that it is on its last legs. Last year it had no money to pay staff, provide petrol for its trucks or pay its electricity bills at some of its post offices. Months of a violent strike had decimated confidence and customers deserted it in droves. Parcels were opened, items filched, many items just never arrived. The South African post office – an SOE that had last made a profit in 2011 joined South Africa’s other ailing State owned enterprises. In fact the jury is still out on whether or not it’s a going concern. Its financials are a horror story so why would anyone take up a five year contract and vow to make it work.
Carte Blanche goes behind the story to find out how Mark Barnes convinced a group of senior cabinet ministers that the post office is not in fact a liability but an asset with huge potential and he was prepared to take up the challenge.

Press Release:


Posting Mark Barnes
He’s been called ‘brilliant’ and ‘a maverick’ and has just stepped into what he believes is the most exciting challenge of his life. Carte Blanche witnesses his engaging leadership style as we join newly appointed SA Post Office CEO Mark Barnes on surprise visits to depot employees and more. Will he succeed in his plan to turn the beleaguered parastatal into a slick operation within five years?


Script:


MARK BARNES FINAL SCRIPT SATURDAY 30th Jan 2016

Commentary One
In 2014 a four-month long strike almost crippled the post office. The mail piled up. Customers left - Senior Manager Thomas Mokoatlo has had first hand experience of the labour instability

Thomas
There are times when you shed tears and wish you were not part of the place
but only way to grow – once thru hurdles …trying to achieve whatever I can

Commentary two
Chris Yelland and a group of specialist magazine publishers had to make contingency plans or risk losing their livelihoods

Chris Yelland
I will give you an example, if you are a conference organizer you may advertise conference in April in June they have spent money for nothing and they don’t want to pay us.

Commentary three
So the publishers asked ICASA to censure the Post office. The post office hit back with an unusual defence, and the publishers still have no answers

Chris Yelland
Effectively they are claiming force Majeur – or an act of god himself. Our response is that this was certainly not an act of god it was an act of poor management by the management itself.

Commentary four
Since then the post office has been in ICU. Clouded by corruption, and management instability. Workers are owed back pay, suppliers haven’t been paid. And its just reported a R1.4 billion rand loss

LINK
For Bryanston residents this was our post office …terse notice on the door and for the last few months we have been wandering around trying to find our mail

Commentary five
Mike McKeowan manages this fly fishing shop where they sell and repair these high quality fly rods. Their business once relied on speed services and registered mail at the Bryanston post office

Mike
I arrived at the Post Office with my number for the international parcel – the guy asked if I had a torch with me- guy with a cell phone and we went into the back to find the parcel



Commentary six
The post office failed to pay the rent so the landlord switched off the lights. Mike knew it was time to abandon the post office. He wont go back

Mike
So they had been running on the generator, now they didn’t have petrol for the generator. The staff were very concerned that the area manager didn’t care about it either

Commentary seven
These days its hard to find someone who cares about or trusts the post office, so it comes as a surprise that a Harvard educated, former investment banker is championing its potential

MARK BARNES
Derek we are this close to business, we are just around the corner man, and you could go there to get your social grant, if there was paper to print it on, to renew your license, and you could go there to download anti-retrovirals its just in a bad mood we need to give it a chance

Commentary eight
Three weeks ago Mark Barnes started his five- year contract as the new CEO. Some of his friends were astonished

Mark
Most of them go what do you want to do that for Barnsey? You have a nice life
And my response to all of us that have something to offer – whatever it is a skill, a bit of money some thought processes – go find something difficult to do. If you can teach, teach somebody … go write a business plan for someone who can’t do it

Commentary nine
Difficult- hardly describes this job. Barnes takes over when its losing around a hundred million rand a month. He has been called a maverick, but can this maverick fix it?

Mark
I don’t know what that means, but I love it, its cool to be called a maverick

Commentary ten
His career took off at Standard Bank. Recently this actuarial science graduate founded his own investment company

Derek
You see potential in post bank don’t you?
Mark
Absolutely! Its central to our forward thinking. If you look at the companies that have the highest valuations - I am talking about Facebook and so on, what have they got? Its because they have got a client accumulation strategy which is winning. We have de facto the biggest client base in South Africa – we know your address man so be nice to us
Derek
I better watch it
Mark
Or you wont get your letters at Christmas!

Commentary eleven
Last year Deputy president Cyril Ramaphosa inherited the troubled State owned entity

LINK
Mark kept a close eye on the disintegration of the Post office even writing some possible solutions saying hell I would even like to give it a shot myself

MARK
I started off wanting to be an advisor but the more I got involved in this thing eventually I wanted to do it

Commentary twelve
By May 2015, the post office announced a plan to cut 5000 jobs and close down hundreds of post offices. That is when Mark approached Cyril Ramaphosa

Mark Barnes
And I engaged with government and I said if you do that you are going to take a defunct loss making dysfunctional organization and all you will do is make it a smaller defunct loss making organization. What about a growth strategy?

Commentary thirteen
They listened, and his plans got the nod. But a white male capitalist is a rare breed at a State owned enterprise

MARK
to be frank that has never been discussed with me. All the discussions I have had with government have been beyond my expectations. Really!

Derek
My doubts at the back of my mind are political interference?
Mark
Why would they interfere? Who would stop this? What’s not virtuous about this? I would argue at the risk of being immodest that if this works they wont stop this it will be copied …
Derek
It’s a test case?
Mark
Ya it is a test case and I feel the extraordinary weight of that responsibility I really do!

Commentary fourteen
This is Witspos, the biggest clearing depot in the Southern Hemisphere. The last time we filmed here was in 1997, when Carte Blanche had caught workers on camera stealing the post.

“Perfect, Its mine”

At the time these machines sorting machines were hard at work. Now they are broken and there is no money to fix them. And that is Barnes biggest challenge- finding the money to seal off the past and recapitalize the future

MARK
The SAPO mustn’t wake up in the morning and think it has entitlement and rights.
So when I go to government and say I want 100 marbles …they mustn’t say give it to me because I am the post office they must give it to me because that is the best way that they can spend the money

Commentary fifteen
There is also no money for increases and promises that were made to workers have not all been honoured, says SA postal workers union Vulture Ntuluki

Vulture
Promises were made, agreements were there and never implemented

Commentary Sixteen
On Tuesday when Mark visited Witspos for the first time the staff were overwhelmed

Up Sound staff go crazy

Mark its insane! Fantastic!

Commentary seventeen
Some staff told us they haven’t met a CEO in 15 years.

STAMP UPSOUND

He hopes to work closely with the unions

MARK
So we need to sit in the middle and say ok here is the backlog here is the line this is how deep the hole is and then we are going to fill the hole together and then we are going to cut a deal and then we are going to find an economic balance between the future and the past but if you stop me going forward that line just goes down a bit and at some point the vultures in private enterprise that can’t wait to eat off the carcass of the post office will come to feed

Up sound
Hi I am Mark Barnes ……..together

Mark
You should listen really listen not politely listen – politeness has very little place in my life. Distilled essence is far more valuable than long reports so since I got here the reports are starting to get shorter already, second point - You can’t as a single individual drag 30 000 people along – 30 000 people can incrementally bring one another along so you need to instill a faith

Commentary eighteen
These are some of the lessons he has learnt over three decades in business

Mark
The most important lesson of all – the present value of the truth is far less painful always than the deferred consequence of the lie, so face it deal with it. When I came here I found everything delegated up to me, so I delegate everything down with force
Derek
Isn’t that the first mistake
Mark
If you delegate with respect there will be mistakes but the punishment for not making a call at all, is less severe that is how we are going to run this place

THOMAS
And he said we gonna fix it from the bottom up and I think that is the biggest motivation we can get from a leader

DEREK
How are you going to regain the faith of your customers?
By doing little things right every day …
Derek
Time span do you see
Six months before we reach accords, another six before the brand restores its faith in the public domain and in 3 years time we should be humming!

THE END
